assessment: The ask Andrew is holding changed category this fire, and that is the whole content of this cycle. For four days it has been a correctness bug in what the console DISPLAYS -- a grid phase, an endpoint, two counters measured over different populations. Reading the sibling branch of the same function (rules.md rev 16 rows 5 and 6, applied for the second consecutive fire) turned up a fourth clause in the same file whose consequence is of a different order: emit_build_status.py's next-expected advance at lines 279-283 exits the moment nxt >= t0 WITHOUT re-testing in_schedule, so next_expected_at is published outside the job's own window -- measured on two of three jobs in this build, premarket advertising 11:00:44 today against a 07:00-09:00 window whose true next slot is Monday 07:00, evening advertising 11:30:38 against a window that does not open until 15:30 -- and the 'late' test at line 301 is taken against that same out-of-window nxt. Simulated forward from this build's own figures, a harvest that stops at its last Friday slot reads 'healthy' for 66.7 h (intraday), 71.2 h (premarket) and 66.7 h (evening) before the console will say 'late'. Today is Friday. harvest_intraday is the only irreversible job on the board -- its own why says a window missed there is history lost to a 200-timestamp rolling buffer -- and if it stops after 15:00 this afternoon the board will report it healthy until Monday 09:40. Right now, in this build, harvest_evening has not run for 13.5 h, renders 24 na and nothing else, and reads healthy. So the three display clauses and this one are no longer the same kind of ask: the first three mean Andrew cannot trust the numbers, this one means the monitor cannot tell him the harvest stopped. Said against this lane: the first reading of this finding was stronger and WRONG -- that 'late' was structurally unreachable -- and it was falsified by this lane's own counterfactual within the same fire, which showed late does latch once the window reopens and is missed by a cadence. The corrected claim is a bounded blind interval, not an unreachable state, and that is what the item says. Nothing else moved: trunk 1a05afa for 21.4 days, zero events or tasks by anyone but this lane, phase 1a held at 95 with its kind:proof deliverable still TODO, the executor leg still has no live carrier, and the courier leg is alive on an eleventh advancing dispatch sha. The decision has not widened -- it is still one call on one file -- but its cost of delay now includes a weekend of silence on the irreversible job rather than a wrong number on a strip.

items.title: A FOURTH clause on the same one-file ask, and the first that makes the monitor silent rather than wrong: a stopped harvest reads healthy for up to 67 hours, and today is Friday
items.why: This is the SAME decision as c-0022.1 -- one call on dashboard/emit_build_status.py -- with a fourth measured clause, and it is raised again inside 24 h only because the clause changes what delay costs. Read verbatim from source this fire (file unchanged for 29.8 d): job_entry sets nxt = last_run + cadence and then runs `while nxt < t0 and not in_schedule(nxt, job): nxt += cad`. The loop exits as soon as nxt >= t0 WHETHER OR NOT that instant is inside the job's window, so next_expected_at is published out-of-window for any job whose gap spans outside its own schedule. Measured on this build, two of three jobs: harvest_premarket last ran 08:30:44 and publishes next_expected_at 2026-10-02T11:00:44-05:00 against a 07:00-09:00 window -- its true next in-schedule slot is 2026-10-05T07:00; harvest_evening last ran 2026-10-01T21:30:38 and publishes 2026-10-02T11:30:38-05:00 against a 15:30-21:30 window. harvest_intraday's value is in-window only because it ran 1 s before the build. All three published values reproduce exactly from source arithmetic (evening's requires t0 to carry a sub-second fraction, which is itself an admission that the published generated_at is a truncation of the instant actually used). The consequence is the status line, not the field: status reaches 'late' only when `t0 > nxt + cad`, and nxt is pinned at or after t0 until the job's window reopens. Simulated forward from this build's own configuration, a harvest that stops at its last Friday slot reads 'healthy' for 66.7 h (harvest_intraday), 71.2 h (harvest_premarket) and 66.7 h (harvest_evening). harvest_intraday is the only irreversible job on the board; a window missed there is history lost. This is live, not hypothetical: harvest_evening is 13.5 h without a run in this build, renders 24 na and nothing else, and reads healthy. STATED AGAINST THIS LANE: the first form of this finding claimed 'late' was unreachable altogether; this lane's own counterfactual falsified that inside the same fire -- late does latch, from about 38 h after a weekday stop, and persists. The claim is a bounded blind interval, not an unreachable state. Why it is Andrew's and not this lane's: unchanged from c-0022.1 -- dashboard/ is this lane's path, but the file is invoked by scripts/daily.py and the post-commit hook every thirty minutes, this session can neither RUN it nor run pytest to prove a write, and the three-week-old next_expected_at convention is a contract with the console page.
items.acceptance: Andrew says fix it with the other three clauses or does not. If fixed: (1) the next-expected advance continues past t0 until in_schedule(nxt) is true, so next_expected_at is never published at an instant the job's own schedule excludes -- checked on a build taken OUTSIDE every job's window (e.g. any build between 09:00 and 15:30 CDT, where premarket and evening are both idle), where premarket must publish the next weekday 07:00 slot and evening the same day's 15:30 slot; (2) 'late' is decided against the first in-schedule slot the job actually missed, not against a slot at or after the build clock, so a job with no run for more than one cadence INSIDE its own window reads late within one build, and a job stopped at its last Friday slot reads late by the first build of the next trading day rather than 67 h later; (3) the emitter states in a comment which instant next_expected_at denotes and what 'late' is measured against -- the same comment c-0022.1's clauses (b) and (c), t-20260929-expected-24h-fencepost and t-20260930-window-mask-keys-on-left-edge all ask for, so one comment can discharge all of them; (4) verified by RE-RUNNING emit, not by reading the diff -- the last fire's unattributed slot in intraday's expected_in_24h reconstruction (14 by hand against 13 published) is still open and is only resolvable by running it. No run history is edited, no status is hand-set, and no beat strip is widened. Evidence: e-000225 (source verbatim plus the three-job reproduction and the forward simulation), e-000223 and e-000224 from the previous fire, and bus m-20261002-1118.

items.title: The FIFTH build moved a false miss onto intraday while premarket's persists a third build and evening's strip stays entirely dark -- five strips in one day, none of them trusted
items.why: Against the end goal this matters because phase 1a is the head of the critical path 1a->2->3->6 and its kind:proof deliverable is held at wip by exactly these published misses. Five builds today at 07:00, 08:00, 09:00, 10:00 and 11:00 CDT, and the strips disagree with each other and with their own file. The 10:00 build published intraday 22 na / 2 ok with NO miss; the 11:00 build publishes 20 na / 3 ok / 1 MISS on the same run history, so a false miss has MIGRATED ONTO intraday -- the second migration recorded in two days (e-000222 was the first) and now on the critical job. harvest_premarket's single miss persists a THIRD consecutive build, slot-verified clean at e-000221. harvest_evening renders 24 na and nothing else for a SECOND consecutive build while the SAME file publishes runs_24h 13 for it -- two halves of one artefact contradicting each other, which is why e-000224 is still the strongest demonstration on the board and this build does not displace it. First-hand this fire: data/results/run_history.jsonl staged and read, 893 records; in the trailing 24 h from the build clock, mode intraday has 14 runs all ok (including 09:01:31 and 09:31:27, both ok, 37,566 and 19,261 rows), premarket 4 all ok, evening 13 all ok. ZERO failures in any mode. So every miss and every na on all three strips this build is published over a run log with no failure in it. Which of the five strips published today is correct remains UNDECIDABLE from the artefact, and this item says so rather than privileging the newest or the most extreme reading.
items.acceptance: Resolution is c-0023.1 / c-0022.1, which is Andrew's -- this item asks for no separate decision and no new task. It is checked when a single weekday build publishes a strip whose every non-na cell is reproducible at zero residual from run_history.jsonl under a stated mask, with the number of non-na cells stated alongside, and the same strip reproduces on the next build of the same day with no cell migrating between jobs. Evidence: e-000226, and e-000219 / e-000221 / e-000222 / e-000224 for the four earlier strips.

items.title: The sibling-branch read paid for a second consecutive fire, and the stronger version of its finding was wrong -- record both halves
items.why: This is a method item for this lane, not work for anyone else, and it is in the cycle because the same move has now produced the two largest findings of two consecutive fires and because its failure mode showed up in the same breath. The previous fire finally ran a deferred source read, found nothing new in the thing it had deferred, and then found a third defect by reading the SIBLING branch of the same comparison -- the side five fires had taken on trust. This fire applied that deliberately to the fields NOBODY had read in a function read three times (next_expected_at, status) and found the fourth clause, which is the one that matters most. Generalisable form, worth a KB row when the freeze lifts: WHEN A FUNCTION HAS BEEN READ FOR ONE FIELD AND RE-READ FOR A SECOND, THE DEFECT IS MOST LIKELY IN THE FIELD NOBODY HAS ASKED ABOUT -- enumerate every field the function returns and name which have been checked, because a field with no open question against it is not a field that has been verified. THE OTHER HALF, which is why this item exists rather than a self-congratulatory note: the first form of this fire's finding was that 'late' was structurally unreachable, and it was falsified by this lane's own forward simulation within the same fire. The simulation was cheap (one loop over t0) and it was only run because the claim was about to be pushed to Andrew's phone. The lesson is the pairing, not either half: read the unasked sibling, THEN try to falsify the strongest form of what you found before it leaves the session.
items.acceptance: Captured as a KB lesson with both halves -- the sibling-field enumeration and the falsify-before-push control -- once t-20260908-kb-into-git lands and the write freeze lifts. Until then it is recorded here and in the dispatcher receipt's kb block, and nothing is written to C:\Shared\lessons-learned-kb or to the Drive tier. Checked by: the KB freeze lifting and the row appearing with both halves, or by a later fire citing this item when it enumerates a function's unread fields before re-reading it.
